title: HORUS Process Engine process definition, schema version 1
description: A process as authored in YAML or JSON and deployed with POST /api/bpm/processes/v1/definitions. Steps run in list order unless next says otherwise. Checks that need the whole document or other data (every next target exists, every non-end path reaches an end, rule sets and adapters exist, the guardrail contract) run in the engine at deploy time; this schema checks structure only.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this definition format. Documents written for an older schema version deploy forever.

process.description: Definition key, unique within a tenant, kebab-case. Deploying the same key again creates the next version.

expressionLanguage.description: Language of every expression in this document (gateway conditions). Only urn:horus-bpm:expr:v1 is accepted in schema version 1; FEEL arrives with a later schema version (ADR-0017, ADR-0019). Stored with the version.

variables.description: Optional declaration of instance variables and their types, used for deploy-time checks of ${instance.x} references.

diagram.description: Optional layout: node positions, edge waypoints and lanes, in the format of definition-layout.v1.schema.json (urn:horus-bpm:schema:definition-layout:v1), checked by the engine at import. The engine stores it as a layout revision and removes it from the stored definition, so it is never part of the definition hash and changing it needs no approval (ADR-0013).

nodeId.description: Step id. Any BPMN-style id (an XML ID without a colon: a letter or underscore, then letters, digits, underscore, dot or hyphen), so ids of imported BPMN models are kept as they are (ADR-0017). Kebab-case is the recommended style for hand-written definitions.

duration.description: ISO 8601 duration, for example PT30S, PT5M, PT4H, P1D.

variableRef.description: Reference to an instance variable: ${instance.<path>}, where path is one or more identifiers separated by dots (${instance.customer.segment}). The reference must be the whole string, so the value keeps its type (a money object stays a money object); there is no interpolation inside a longer string and no escape. The root instance is the only root in schema version 1; other roots are reserved. The value is read when the step starts; a missing variable fails the step with INPUT_VARIABLE_MISSING and opens an incident.

inputValue.description: A variable reference, or a literal. A string containing ${ that is not exactly one reference is rejected.

inputs.description: Bounded input map passed to the step; only these values reach a rule set, a handler or an agent.

next.description: Id of the following step. Defaults to the next step in the list.

retry.description: max is the number of retries after the first attempt, so max 2 gives 3 attempts in total. backoff is the delay before each retry.

signalName.description: The name a signal event and a broadcast match on, within one tenant.

signal.description: A signal start event: a broadcast of this name starts an instance.

condition.description: A conditional start event: the instance starts only when this condition is true for the start variables.

signal.description: A signal end event: broadcasts this signal when reached.

condition.description: Passes at once when true on arrival, otherwise waits until a change of the instance variables makes it true.

fourEyes.description: The identities that started the instance or completed earlier steps of it cannot complete this task.

form.description: How the task is completed: a form key registered by the host, a JSON Schema with display hints (format of task-form.v1.schema.json $defs/hints, urn:horus-bpm:schema:task-form:v1), or a link to the host's own screen. A link must be relative or match tasks.form-link-origins, checked at import.

escalation.description: Up to three levels. The first fires at the due time plus its after, each later one its after of working time past the previous (PRE-178 to PRE-180).

mode.description: local runs inside the current transaction and may write only to the host database; remote runs as an Async Wait-State (ADR-0008).

timeout.description: Remote mode only. Bounds the call and sets the lease (timeout plus jobs.lease-margin). Defaults to adapters.default-timeout (PT30S).

compensate.description: Handler that undoes this step, idempotent by attemptId, or manual to raise an incident instead.

maskedInputs.description: Inputs the agent receives in plain text but history and the review task keep only as keyed fingerprints (hmac:<keyId>:<hex>), or *** when no masking key is configured. Each name must be one of inputs.

fieldTitles.description: Localised titles of the step's input and output fields for the review screen: inputs and outputs, each a map of field name to a map of language tag to title (up to 100 fields, 120 characters a title). Labels only; no check reads them. The review task returns them as fieldTitles.

outputSchema.description: The JSON Schema the agent output must satisfy, inline, so the definition hash and its approval cover it. The engine default supports a subset (type, properties, required, additionalProperties true or false, enum, const, the numeric bounds, minLength, maxLength, items, minItems, maxItems, and the annotations title, description, default, examples and mask); any other keyword is refused at import.

decision.description: Rule set evaluated on the agent output. It must have hitPolicy first or unique, output allow: boolean and may output reasons: list<string>; checked at deploy time.

onViolation.description: route-to-human (needs reviewer) opens a four-eyes review task; fail fails the step's job.

reviewer.description: Who reviews a refused answer. The review is always four-eyes and cannot be switched off.

memory.description: Facts from earlier agent steps of the same instance that this step's agent receives: only the listed fields of each step's recorded result (an accepted answer, or a reviewer's answer after a refusal), resolved once when the step is reached and the same on every attempt. The host bounds the entries (agents.memory.max-entries, 16) and the size (agents.memory.max-bytes, 16 KiB of canonical JSON); a larger memory fails the step with AGENT_MEMORY_TOO_LARGE, and a required entry with no recorded result fails it with AGENT_MEMORY_MISSING.

from.description: An upstream agentTask step of this process whose output schema declares the fields.

fields.description: Field paths of that step's output, dot-separated for nested objects, at most four levels. Wildcards are never allowed.

as.description: The name the fields are passed under.

required.description: Without a recorded result, true fails the step with AGENT_MEMORY_MISSING; false leaves the entry out and history lists it as missing.

includeMasked.description: Allows fields the source step's output schema marks mask: true. The agent receives them in plain text, history keeps keyed fingerprints, and the approval shows the flag.

branches.description: Checked in order; the first true condition wins. Conditions use the Rule Engine expression language over instance variables.

default.description: Step taken when no branch matches.

next.description: A list forks one token per entry. A single id, or none, after a join.
The catch events (message, signal, timer, conditional) or receive tasks the gateway waits on; the first to fire wins and the others are cancelled.

until.description: An instant (RFC 3339 date-time) or a reference to a datetime variable.

calendar.description: Business calendar for duration; omitted means elapsed time.

version.description: Pin a version; omitted means the latest at call time.

inputs.description: What the child receives, by the child's variable name; nothing else is passed.

outputs.description: What comes back: the parent's variable name to the child's variable it is set from. Nothing else the child holds is copied.
